recommendation: Keep the fix. It restores a previously applied R5 clarification after the actor refactor without changing cardinalities or adding a new invariant.
issue_request: FHIR-27779 was a Published/Persuasive R5 FHIR-core Consent clarification requesting the comment say that a Consent without performer is a statement of preference by the subject and is not in force.
initial_application: Git commit 374f01bb8e originally added the requested sentence to the old Consent.performer comment in source/consent/consent-spreadsheet.xml. The later source migration and Consent.performer-to-grantor/grantee refactor left current source without the FHIR-27779 clarification.
additional_context: FHIR-31906 converted Consent.performer into Consent.grantor and Consent.grantee and introduced the current grantee comment about fully computable Consent actors. Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, and FHIR-11061 supports the grantor/grantee party distinction. No Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that supersedes the Jira/source-history conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml so the Consent.grantee comment states that a Consent without any listed grantor or grantee may be used as a subject preference statement and is not in force.
source_changes: source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml: updated the Consent.grantee comment to carry the FHIR-27779 preference/not-in-force meaning in the current grantor/grantee model.
